security_audit.summary: All 37 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, expected browser commands, benign example URLs, and a comment. One medium semantic risk remains: the fallback installation uses a mutable package version globally, increasing supply-chain and host impact.

remediation.issue: The fallback installation uses a mutable latest version with global scope.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed exact version and prefer a project-local install. Require user confirmation before installing or changing global packages.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Flows with Playwright CLI
content.value_statement: Manual browser inspection makes reliable automation scripts difficult to author. This skill uses Playwright CLI to navigate pages, capture snapshots, and verify selectors.
actual_capabilities: Opens browser sessions and navigates to specified web pages.
Captures page snapshots with element references for later interactions.
Clicks, types, fills, selects, checks, and hovers over page elements.
Evaluates page expressions to inspect titles, text, and element attributes.
Identifies stable selectors and cookie consent actions for ScreenCI scripts.
Compares before and after snapshots to reveal page state changes.
limitations: Requires Playwright CLI to be installed globally or available in the current project.
Element references can change after navigation or page updates.
The skill inspects live pages but does not author complete ScreenCI scripts by itself.
Authentication, captchas, and protected environments may require manual access or additional setup.

use_cases.title: Verify a User Journey
use_cases.description: Navigate a live flow, interact with controls, and capture page states before adding an automated test.

use_cases.title: Discover Stable Selectors
use_cases.description: Inspect roles, test identifiers, and attributes to select reliable targets for browser automation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a ScreenCI Recording
use_cases.description: Find consent actions and hidden setup steps before creating a repeatable ScreenCI visual script.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], capture a snapshot, and summarize the page title, main controls, and visible consent banners. Do not submit forms.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner inspection of an unfamiliar page

prompt_templates.title: Test a Simple Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], find [control], activate it, and compare snapshots before and after. Report the resulting page change.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Complete Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the flow from [start URL] to [goal]. Record each action, stable locator, page state, and required consent step.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare ScreenCI Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [URL] for a ScreenCI script. Identify hidden setup actions, resilient selectors, dynamic content risks, and checkpoints for each visible step.

output_examples.input: Inspect the Playwright documentation home page and identify the search control.
output_examples.output: The page loaded successfully. The search control is available by role and accessible name, making it preferable to a generated element reference.

output_examples.input: Compare the page before and after selecting the submit button.
output_examples.output: The second snapshot shows a confirmation message and a disabled submit button. No navigation occurred.

output_examples.input: Find the consent step needed before recording a ScreenCI flow.
output_examples.output: A cookie banner appears after navigation. Use the clearly labeled accept button during hidden setup, then capture a new snapshot.

best_practices: Capture a new snapshot after navigation or any action that changes the page.
Prefer roles, accessible names, and test identifiers over fragile CSS paths.
Confirm the target domain and expected side effects before submitting forms.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse stale element references after the page changes.
Do not enter real credentials or sensitive data into demonstration flows.
Do not install mutable global packages without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: Playwright CLI must be available globally or in the current project. A compatible browser installation may also be required.

faq.question: Can this skill inspect a page without changing it?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the page and capture snapshots without clicking controls or submitting forms.

faq.question: Why do element references sometimes stop working?
faq.answer: References describe a specific page snapshot. Navigation, reloads, or dynamic updates can replace the referenced elements.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, when the browser session has valid access. Authentication setup and secret handling remain the user's responsibility.

faq.question: How does it help with ScreenCI scripts?
faq.answer: It reveals real navigation steps, selectors, consent actions, and page states before script authoring.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically publish or run ScreenCI scripts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on browser inspection and interaction discovery using Playwright CLI.
